They are collected here because\neach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\nstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n\n| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n\n## 18.2 Proof obligations\n\nEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. Open questions\n\n1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\nhours is a genuine seizure risk.\n\n**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\nfewer cells → less throughput. D10's DC balancing is part of this mitigation, not just an\nauto-exposure fix: constant mean luminance is far less provocative than alternating fields.\n\n### 20.2 Delta transfer tensions with the block design (`bf-280`)\n\n**A partially-received file *is* \"a file the receiver already has\"** — so\nresume-after-interruption and delta transfer are one mechanism at two granularities.\n\nBut general delta wants **content-defined chunking** (rolling hash, variable boundaries),\nwhich contradicts I1 (L fixed) and D19 (fixed blocks, K derived). Measure baseline thermal behavior (100% duty, existing test)\n2. Measure duty-cycled behavior (50% duty, new test)\n3. Compare heat generation, decode rates, and completion\n\n## Running the test\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n1. **Cool start** — device rested at room temperature for ≥10 minutes\n2. **Record starting temperature** (Pixel 6: Settings → System → Developer options → Quick settings for dev tools → Thermal)\n3. **Rig server running:**\n   ```bash\n   cd spike && npm install && npm run rig\n   ```\n\n### Physical setup (§13.2 denominator)\n\n- **Mounting:** tripod (or as stable as possible)\n- **Distance:** 30 cm measured\n- **Lighting:** ~300 lux\n- **Screen:** 50%+ brightness\n- **Duration:** minimum 60 minutes, ideal 90–120 minutes\n\n### Test A: Baseline (100% duty)\n\n1. **Sender (this machine):**\n   - URL: `http://localhost:5174/thermal-profile.html`\n   - Mode: Sender\n   - Rung: R2 (v16, 2 packets/tile, nominal)\n   - FPS: 8\n   - Grid: 5×3 = 15 tiles\n   - Module px: 4\n\n2. **Receiver (Pixel 6):**\n   - URL: `http://46.62.187.167:5174/thermal-profile.html` (or localhost if on same machine)\n   - Mode: Receiver\n   - Fragment size L: 256 bytes\n   - Log interval: 30 seconds\n   - Camera: rear-facing, 1920×1080 requested\n\n3. **Run for 60+ minutes**, then export CSV\n\n### Test B: Duty cycle (50%)\n\n1. **Sender (this machine):**\n   - Same configuration as Test A\n\n2. **Receiver (Pixel 6):**\n   - URL: `http://46.62.187.167:5174/thermal-profile-dutycycle.html`\n   - Mode: Receiver\n   - Fragment size L: 256 bytes\n   - Log interval: 30 seconds\n   - Camera: rear-facing, 1920×1080 requested\n   - **Duty cycle:** 50% (automatic: 1s ON, 1s OFF)\n\n3. **Run for 60+ minutes**, then export CSV\n\n## Expected outcomes\n\n### D27 makes three claims:\n\n1. **Heat reduction:** 50% duty roughly halves heat generation\n   - Measured by: proxy through camera fps and decode latency stability\n   - Expected: ~50% reduction in sustained processing rate\n\n2. **Rate reduction:** 50% duty roughly halves the effective rate\n   - Measured by: effective fps (measured fps × 0.5)\n   - Expected: ~50% of baseline throughput\n\n3. **Completion:** Duty cycle finishes where 100% duty may not\n   - Measured by: thermal degradation >30% (R11 trigger)\n   - Expected: baseline degrades >30%, duty cycle stays <30%\n\n### Analysis\n\nAfter collecting both CSV files, run:\n\n```bash\npython spike/plot-thermal-profile-comparison.py <baseline-csv> <dutycycle-csv>\n```\n\nThis generates:\n- Comparison plots (FPS, decode latency, erasure rate)\n- Statistical summary\n- D27 validation assessment\n\n## Success criteria\n\nD27 is **validated** if all three claims hold:\n\n1. ✓ Heat reduction proxy is ~50% (40–60% range)\n2. ✓ Rate reduction is ~50% (40–60% range)\n3. ✓ Duty cycle stays stable (<30% degradation) where baseline degrades (>30%)\n\nD27 is **partially validated** if:\n- Some claims hold but others need investigation\n- Test duration insufficient (need 90–120 minutes)\n\nD27 is **not validated** if:\n- Heat/rate reduction far from 50% (outside 40–60% range)\n- Duty cycle still degrades >30% (may need lower duty %)\n\n## Kill criterion (R11 trigger)\n\n| Observation | Consequence |\n|---|---|\n| **Duty cycle still shows >30% sustained degradation** | D27 mitigation insufficient; need lower duty % or different approach |\n\n## Post-test actions\n\n1. **Update spike-results.md** with measurements\n2. **Update plan.md §18 risk register** (R11, D27)\n3. **Update plan.md §13.1** if performance budgets change\n4. **Close this bead** with commit\n\n## Status\n\n- [x] Duty-cycle thermal profile HTML created\n- [x] Comparison plotting script created\n- [x] Test protocol documented\n- [ ] Baseline thermal profile collected\n- [ ] Duty-cycle thermal profile collected\n- [ ] Analysis completed\n- [ ] Results recorded in spike-results.md\n- [ ] Plan updated if needed"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1e92afa4-3683-470a-82bd-61212380a3cb","uuid":"548cf0e8-71f5-4977-b4b0-df0291c2a472","timestamp":"2026-08-02T07:43:39.204Z"}

60]\n\n### Claim 2: Rate reduction ≈ 50%\n**Measured by:** Effective FPS (measured FPS × 0.5)\n**Expected:** 40–60% reduction vs baseline\n**Validation:** `rate_reduction` in [40, 60]\n\n### Claim 3: Duty cycle completes where 100% duty may not\n**Measured by:** Thermal degradation trigger (>30% FPS/decode degradation)\n**Expected:** Baseline degrades >30%, duty cycle stays <30%\n**Validation:** `abs(dutycycle_fps_deg) < 30` where `abs(baseline_fps_deg) > 30`\n\n**D27 is validated** if all three claims hold.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n### Why pause/resume instead of frame skipping?\nThe implementation pauses/resumes the video element rather than skipping frames in JavaScript because:\n1. **More realistic:** Pausing the video stops the entire camera pipeline, including ISP processing\n2. **Cleaner duty boundary:** 1-second granularity is easier to measure and validate\n3. **Lower overhead:** No JS bookkeeping per frame\n4. **Matches D27's intent:** \"Skipped frame is an erasure\" — paused frames are effectively skipped\n\n### Duty cycle granularity\nCurrent implementation: **1-second ON, 1-second OFF** (50% duty)\n- Easy to observe and verify\n- Sufficient for thermal effects (heat dissipation time constants)\n- Could be tuned (e.g., 2s/2s, 5s/5s) if needed\n\n### Block-granular vs time-granular\nThe task mentions \"block-granular duty cycling.\" In the rig context (no actual fountain code blocks), time-based cycling at 1-second granularity is equivalent:\n- A fountain code block at K=768, L=256B = 192KB\n- At 8 FPS with 15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 256B = ~60 KB/s effective\n- One block ≈ 3 seconds of data\n- 1-second duty cycling is finer than block-granular\n\n## Status\n\n✅ **Infrastructure complete:**\n- Duty-cycle thermal profile HTML created\n-
